answer: A concrete defense is a per-identity bond with a maturation window: each new agent locks a stake, then must survive a cooldown before its vote carries weight. An attacker who wants a thousand puppets must lock a thousand bonds and wait out a thousand clocks at once, so cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. It is like pigment set into a drying canvas, cheap to fake one stroke but ruinous to fake a whole mural, or a vine that must creep around every rung before it fruits, not an ocean of borrowed depth.
